# Plan: Remove Strategy Selection from `entire enable`

## Summary

Remove the interactive strategy selection prompt from `entire enable` and use `manual-commit` as the default. Document the `--strategy` flag as the alternative for users who want `auto-commit`.

## Changes

### 1. Modify `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`

**Update command description (line 56):**
```go
Long: `Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

Uses the manual-commit strategy by default. To use a different strategy:

  entire enable --strategy auto-commit

Strategies: manual-commit (default), auto-commit`,
```

**Simplify `runEnableInteractive()` (lines 277-302):**

Remove the huh.Select form for strategy selection and use the default strategy directly:

```go
func runEnableInteractive(w io.Writer, localDev, _, useLocalSettings, useProjectSettings, forceHooks, setupShell, skipPushSessions, telemetry, disableMultisessionWarning bool) error {
	// Use the default strategy (manual-commit)
	internalStrategy := strategy.DefaultStrategyName
	fmt.Fprintf(w, "Using %s strategy (use --strategy to change)\n\n", internalStrategy)

	// Setup Claude Code hooks (continues from existing line 304)
	hooksInstalled, err := setupClaudeCodeHook(localDev, forceHooks)
	// ... rest unchanged ...
```

### 2. Update `README.md`

**Quick Start section (after line 13):**
Add a comment showing the `--strategy` flag option:

```markdown
cd your-project && entire enable

# Or use a specific strategy
entire enable --strategy auto-commit
```

**Commands Reference table (line 100):**
Update the enable row:
```markdown
| `entire enable` | Enable Entire (uses `manual-commit` by default; use `--strategy` for alternatives) |
```

## Files to Modify

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go` | Remove strategy selection form, update Long description |
| `README.md` | Document `--strategy` flag in Quick Start and Commands Reference |

1. Run `mise run fmt && mise run lint` - ensure no lint errors

3. Manual test:
   - `entire enable` should use manual-commit without prompting for strategy

1→# Entire CLI
     2→
     3→Entire hooks into your git workflow to capture AI agent sessions on every push. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written. Runs locally, stays in your repo.
     4→
     5→## Quick Start
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→# Install via Homebrew (requires SSH access)
     9→brew tap entirehq/tap git@github.com:entirehq/homebrew-entire.git
    10→brew install entirehq/tap/entire
    11→
    12→# Enable in your project
    13→cd your-project && entire enable
    14→
    15→# Check status
    16→entire status
    17→```
    18→
    19→## Typical Workflow
    20→
    21→### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
    22→
    23→```bash
    24→entire enable
    25→```
    26→
    27→This installs Claude Code and git hooks that automatically capture checkpoints whenever Claude Code makes changes. Your code commits stay clean—all session metadata is stored separately.
    28→
    29→### 2. Work with Claude Code
    30→
    31→Just use Claude Code normally. Entire runs in the background, creating checkpoints automatically:
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→entire status  # Check current session status anytime
    35→```
    36→
    37→### 3. Rewind to a Previous Checkpoint
    38→
    39→If you want to undo some changes and go back to an earlier checkpoint:
    40→
    41→```bash
    42→entire rewind
    43→```
    44→
    45→This shows all available checkpoints in the current session. Select one to restore your code to that exact state.
    46→
    47→### 4. Resume a Previous Session
    48→
    49→To see and restore sessions from earlier work:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→entire resume
    53→```
    54→
    55→Lists all past sessions with timestamps. You can view the conversation history or restore the code from any session.
    56→
    57→### 5. Disable Entire (Optional)
    58→
    59→```bash
    60→entire disable
    61→```
    62→
    63→Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
    64→
    65→## Key Concepts
    66→
    67→### Sessions
    68→
    69→A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
    70→
    71→**Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
    72→
    73→Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/sessions` branch.
    74→
    75→### Checkpoints
    76→
    77→A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to—a "save point" in your work.
    78→
    79→**When checkpoints are created:**
    80→- **Manual-commit strategy**: When you make a git commit
    81→- **Auto-commit strategy**: After each agent response
    82→
    83→**Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
    84→
    85→### Strategies
    86→
    87→Entire offers two strategies for capturing your work:
    88→
    89→| Aspect | Manual-Commit | Auto-Commit |
    90→|--------|---------------|-------------|
    91→| Code commits | None on your branch | Created automatically after each agent response |
    92→| Safe on main branch | Yes | No - creates commits |
    93→| Rewind | Always possible, non-destructive | Full rewind on feature branches; logs-only on main |
    94→| Best for | Most workflows - keeps git history clean | Teams wanting automatic code commits |
    95→
    96→## Commands Reference
    97→
    98→| Command | Description |
    99→|---------|-------------|
   100→| `entire enable` | Enable Entire in your repository, install hooks |
   101→| `entire disable` | Remove Entire hooks from repository |
   102→| `entire status` | Show current session and strategy info |
   103→| `entire rewind` | Rewind to a previous checkpoint |
   104→| `entire resume` | Resume a previous session |
   105→| `entire explain` | Explain a session or commit |
   106→| `entire session` | View and manage sessions (list, show details, view logs) |
   107→| `entire version` | Show Entire CLI version |
   108→
   109→## Configuration
   110→
   111→Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
   112→
   113→### settings.json (Project Settings)
   114→
   115→Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
   116→
   117→```json
   118→{
   119→  "strategy": "manual-commit",
   120→  "agent": "claude-code",
   121→  "enabled": true
   122→}
   123→```
   124→
   125→### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
   126→
   127→Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
   128→
   129→```json
   130→{
   131→  "enabled": false,
   132→  "log_level": "debug"
   133→}
   134→```
   135→
   136→### Configuration Options
   137→
   138→| Option | Values | Description |
   139→|--------|--------|-------------|
   140→| `strategy` | `manual-commit`, `auto-commit` | Session capture strategy |
   141→| `enabled` | `true`, `false` | Enable/disable Entire |
   142→| `agent` | `claude-code`, `gemini`, etc. | AI agent to integrate with |
   143→| `log_level` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | Logging verbosity |
   144→| `strategy_options.push_sessions` | `true`, `false` | Auto-push `entire/sessions` branch on git push |
   145→
   146→### Settings Priority
   147→
   148→Local settings override project settings field-by-field. When you run `entire status`, it shows both project and local (effective) settings.
   149→
   150→## Troubleshooting
   151→
   152→### Common Issues
   153→
   154→| Issue | Solution |
   155→|-------|----------|
   156→| "Not a git repository" | Navigate to a git repository first |
   157→| "Entire is disabled" | Run `entire enable` |
   158→| "No rewind points found" | Work with Claude Code and commit (manual-commit) or wait for agent response (auto-commit) |
   159→| "shadow branch conflict" | Run `entire rewind reset --force` |
   160→| "session not found" | Check available sessions with `entire session list` |
   161→
   162→### SSH Authentication Errors
   163→
   164→If you see an error like this when running `entire resume`:
   165→
   166→```
   167→Failed to fetch metadata: failed to fetch entire/sessions from origin: ssh: handshake failed: ssh: unable to authenticate, attempted methods [none publickey], no supported methods remain
   168→```
   169→
   170→This is a [known issue with go-git's SSH handling](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/issues/411). Fix it by adding GitHub's host keys to your known_hosts file:
   171→
   172→```bash
   173→ssh-keyscan -t rsa github.com > ~/.ssh/known_hosts
   174→ssh-keyscan -t ecdsa github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
   175→```
   176→
   177→### Debug Mode
   178→
   179→```bash
   180→# Via environment variable
   181→ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug entire status
   182→
   183→# Or via settings.local.json
   184→{
   185→  "log_level": "debug"
   186→}
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Resetting State
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→# Reset shadow branch for current commit
   193→entire rewind reset --force
   194→
   195→# Disable and re-enable
   196→entire disable && entire enable --force
   197→```
   198→
   199→### Accessibility
   200→
   201→For screen reader users, enable accessible mode:
   202→
   203→```bash
   204→export ACCESSIBLE=1
   205→entire enable
   206→```
   207→
   208→This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive TUI elements.
   209→
   210→## Development
   211→
   212→This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.
   213→
   214→### Prerequisites
   215→
   216→- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
   217→
   218→### Getting Started
   219→
   220→```bash
   221→# Clone the repository
   222→git clone <repo-url>
   223→cd cli
   224→
   225→# Install dependencies (including Go)
   226→mise install
   227→
   228→# Build the CLI
   229→mise run build
   230→```
   231→
   232→### Common Tasks
   233→
   234→```bash
   235→# Run tests
   236→mise run test
   237→
   238→# Run integration tests
   239→mise run test:integration
   240→
   241→# Run all tests (unit + integration, CI mode)
   242→mise run test:ci
   243→
   244→# Lint the code
   245→mise run lint
   246→
   247→# Format the code
   248→mise run fmt
   249→```
   250→
   251→### Project Structure
   252→
   253→- `cmd/entire/` - Main CLI entry point
   254→- `cmd/entire/cli/` - CLI utilities and helpers
   255→- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/` - Command implementations
   256→- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/` - Session checkpoint strategies
   257→- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/` - Checkpoint storage abstractions
   258→- `cmd/entire/cli/session/` - Session state management
   259→- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` - Integration tests
   260→
   261→## Getting Help
   262→
   263→```bash
   264→entire --help              # General help
   265→entire <command> --help    # Command-specific help
   266→```
   267→
   268→- **GitHub Issues:** Report bugs or request features at https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues
   269→- **Contributing:** See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines

1→package strategy
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"fmt"
     5→	"sort"
     6→	"sync"
     7→)
     8→
     9→var (
    10→	registryMu sync.RWMutex
    11→	registry   = make(map[string]Factory)
    12→)
    13→
    14→// Factory creates a new strategy instance
    15→type Factory func() Strategy
    16→
    17→// Register adds a strategy factory to the registry.
    18→// This is typically called from init() functions in strategy implementations.
    19→func Register(name string, factory Factory) {
    20→	registryMu.Lock()
    21→	defer registryMu.Unlock()
    22→	registry[name] = factory
    23→}
    24→
    25→// Get retrieves a strategy by name.
    26→// Returns an error if the strategy is not registered.
    27→func Get(name string) (Strategy, error) {
    28→	registryMu.RLock()
    29→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    30→
    31→	factory, ok := registry[name]
    32→	if !ok {
    33→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown strategy: %s (available: %v)", name, List())
    34→	}
    35→
    36→	return factory(), nil
    37→}
    38→
    39→// List returns all registered strategy names in sorted order.
    40→func List() []string {
    41→	registryMu.RLock()
    42→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    43→
    44→	names := make([]string, 0, len(registry))
    45→	for name := range registry {
    46→		names = append(names, name)
    47→	}
    48→	sort.Strings(names)
    49→	return names
    50→}
    51→
    52→// Strategy name constants
    53→const (
    54→	StrategyNameDual         = "dual"   // Legacy name (auto-commit)
    55→	StrategyNameShadow       = "shadow" // Legacy name (manual-commit)
    56→	StrategyNameManualCommit = "manual-commit"
    57→	StrategyNameAutoCommit   = "auto-commit"
    58→)
    59→
    60→// DefaultStrategyName is the name of the default strategy.
    61→// Manual-commit is the recommended strategy for most workflows.
    62→const DefaultStrategyName = StrategyNameManualCommit
    63→
    64→// Default returns the default strategy.
    65→// Falls back to returning nil if no strategies are registered.
    66→func Default() Strategy {
    67→	s, err := Get(DefaultStrategyName)
    68→	if err != nil {
    69→		// Fallback: return the first registered strategy
    70→		names := List()
    71→		if len(names) > 0 {
    72→			s, _ = Get(names[0]) //nolint:errcheck // Fallback to first strategy, error already handled above
    73→		}
    74→	}
    75→	return s
    76→}
    77→
    78→// NormalizeStrategyName maps legacy strategy names to current names.
    79→// These are the strategy names used during initial development and are kept for backwards
    80→// compatibility
    81→func NormalizeStrategyName(name string) string {
    82→	switch name {
    83→	case StrategyNameDual:
    84→		return StrategyNameAutoCommit
    85→	case StrategyNameShadow:
    86→		return StrategyNameManualCommit
    87→	default:
    88→		return name
    89→	}
    90→}
    91→
    92→// IsLegacyStrategyName returns true for names that should be mapped.
    93→func IsLegacyStrategyName(name string) bool {
    94→	return name == StrategyNameDual || name == StrategyNameShadow
    95→}

1→# Entire CLI
     2→
     3→Entire hooks into your git workflow to capture AI agent sessions on every push. Sessions are indexed alongside commits, creating a searchable record of how code was written. Runs locally, stays in your repo.
     4→
     5→## Quick Start
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→# Install via Homebrew (requires SSH access)
     9→brew tap entirehq/tap git@github.com:entirehq/homebrew-entire.git
    10→brew install entirehq/tap/entire
    11→
    12→# Enable in your project
    13→cd your-project && entire enable
    14→
    15→# Check status
    16→entire status
    17→```
    18→
    19→## Typical Workflow
    20→
    21→### 1. Enable Entire in Your Repository
    22→
    23→```bash
    24→entire enable
    25→```
    26→
    27→This installs Claude Code and git hooks that automatically capture checkpoints whenever Claude Code makes changes. Your code commits stay clean—all session metadata is stored separately.
    28→
    29→### 2. Work with Claude Code
    30→
    31→Just use Claude Code normally. Entire runs in the background, creating checkpoints automatically:
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→entire status  # Check current session status anytime
    35→```
    36→
    37→### 3. Rewind to a Previous Checkpoint
    38→
    39→If you want to undo some changes and go back to an earlier checkpoint:
    40→
    41→```bash
    42→entire rewind
    43→```
    44→
    45→This shows all available checkpoints in the current session. Select one to restore your code to that exact state.
    46→
    47→### 4. Resume a Previous Session
    48→
    49→To see and restore sessions from earlier work:
    50→
    51→```bash
    52→entire resume
    53→```
    54→
    55→Lists all past sessions with timestamps. You can view the conversation history or restore the code from any session.
    56→
    57→### 5. Disable Entire (Optional)
    58→
    59→```bash
    60→entire disable
    61→```
    62→
    63→Removes the git hooks. Your code and commit history remain untouched.
    64→
    65→## Key Concepts
    66→
    67→### Sessions
    68→
    69→A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
    70→
    71→**Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
    72→
    73→Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/sessions` branch.
    74→
    75→### Checkpoints
    76→
    77→A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to—a "save point" in your work.
    78→
    79→**When checkpoints are created:**
    80→- **Manual-commit strategy**: When you make a git commit
    81→- **Auto-commit strategy**: After each agent response
    82→
    83→**Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
    84→
    85→### Strategies
    86→
    87→Entire offers two strategies for capturing your work:
    88→
    89→| Aspect | Manual-Commit | Auto-Commit |
    90→|--------|---------------|-------------|
    91→| Code commits | None on your branch | Created automatically after each agent response |
    92→| Safe on main branch | Yes | No - creates commits |
    93→| Rewind | Always possible, non-destructive | Full rewind on feature branches; logs-only on main |
    94→| Best for | Most workflows - keeps git history clean | Teams wanting automatic code commits |
    95→
    96→## Commands Reference
    97→
    98→| Command | Description |
    99→|---------|-------------|
   100→| `entire enable` | Enable Entire in your repository, install hooks |
   101→| `entire disable` | Remove Entire hooks from repository |
   102→| `entire status` | Show current session and strategy info |
   103→| `entire rewind` | Rewind to a previous checkpoint |
   104→| `entire resume` | Resume a previous session |
   105→| `entire explain` | Explain a session or commit |
   106→| `entire session` | View and manage sessions (list, show details, view logs) |
   107→| `entire version` | Show Entire CLI version |
   108→
   109→## Configuration
   110→
   111→Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
   112→
   113→### settings.json (Project Settings)
   114→
   115→Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
   116→
   117→```json
   118→{
   119→  "strategy": "manual-commit",
   120→  "agent": "claude-code",
   121→  "enabled": true
   122→}
   123→```
   124→
   125→### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
   126→
   127→Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
   128→
   129→```json
   130→{
   131→  "enabled": false,
   132→  "log_level": "debug"
   133→}
   134→```
   135→
   136→### Configuration Options
   137→
   138→| Option | Values | Description |
   139→|--------|--------|-------------|
   140→| `strategy` | `manual-commit`, `auto-commit` | Session capture strategy |
   141→| `enabled` | `true`, `false` | Enable/disable Entire |
   142→| `agent` | `claude-code`, `gemini`, etc. | AI agent to integrate with |
   143→| `log_level` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | Logging verbosity |
   144→| `strategy_options.push_sessions` | `true`, `false` | Auto-push `entire/sessions` branch on git push |
   145→
   146→### Settings Priority
   147→
   148→Local settings override project settings field-by-field. When you run `entire status`, it shows both project and local (effective) settings.
   149→
   150→## Troubleshooting
   151→
   152→### Common Issues
   153→
   154→| Issue | Solution |
   155→|-------|----------|
   156→| "Not a git repository" | Navigate to a git repository first |
   157→| "Entire is disabled" | Run `entire enable` |
   158→| "No rewind points found" | Work with Claude Code and commit (manual-commit) or wait for agent response (auto-commit) |
   159→| "shadow branch conflict" | Run `entire rewind reset --force` |
   160→| "session not found" | Check available sessions with `entire session list` |
   161→
   162→### SSH Authentication Errors
   163→
   164→If you see an error like this when running `entire resume`:
   165→
   166→```
   167→Failed to fetch metadata: failed to fetch entire/sessions from origin: ssh: handshake failed: ssh: unable to authenticate, attempted methods [none publickey], no supported methods remain
   168→```
   169→
   170→This is a [known issue with go-git's SSH handling](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/issues/411). Fix it by adding GitHub's host keys to your known_hosts file:
   171→
   172→```bash
   173→ssh-keyscan -t rsa github.com > ~/.ssh/known_hosts
   174→ssh-keyscan -t ecdsa github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
   175→```
   176→
   177→### Debug Mode
   178→
   179→```bash
   180→# Via environment variable
   181→ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug entire status
   182→
   183→# Or via settings.local.json
   184→{
   185→  "log_level": "debug"
   186→}
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Resetting State
   190→
   191→```bash
   192→# Reset shadow branch for current commit
   193→entire rewind reset --force
   194→
   195→# Disable and re-enable
   196→entire disable && entire enable --force
   197→```
   198→
   199→### Accessibility
   200→
   201→For screen reader users, enable accessible mode:
   202→
   203→```bash
   204→export ACCESSIBLE=1
   205→entire enable
   206→```
   207→
   208→This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive TUI elements.
   209→
   210→## Development
   211→
   212→This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.
   213→
   214→### Prerequisites
   215→
   216→- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
   217→
   218→### Getting Started
   219→
   220→```bash
   221→# Clone the repository
   222→git clone <repo-url>
   223→cd cli
   224→
   225→# Install dependencies (including Go)
   226→mise install
   227→
   228→# Build the CLI
   229→mise run build
   230→```
   231→
   232→### Common Tasks
   233→
   234→```bash
   235→# Run tests
   236→mise run test
   237→
   238→# Run integration tests
   239→mise run test:integration
   240→
   241→# Run all tests (unit + integration, CI mode)
   242→mise run test:ci
   243→
   244→# Lint the code
   245→mise run lint
   246→
   247→# Format the code
   248→mise run fmt
   249→```
   250→
   251→### Project Structure
   252→
   253→- `cmd/entire/` - Main CLI entry point
   254→- `cmd/entire/cli/` - CLI utilities and helpers
   255→- `cmd/entire/cli/commands/` - Command implementations
   256→- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/` - Session checkpoint strategies
   257→- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/` - Checkpoint storage abstractions
   258→- `cmd/entire/cli/session/` - Session state management
   259→- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` - Integration tests
   260→
   261→## Getting Help
   262→
   263→```bash
   264→entire --help              # General help
   265→entire <command> --help    # Command-specific help
   266→```
   267→
   268→- **GitHub Issues:** Report bugs or request features at https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues

| `--strategy <name>` | Strategy to use: `manual-commit` (default) or `auto-commit` |
| `--force`, `-f` | Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first) |
| `--local` | Write settings to `settings.local.json` instead of `settings.json` |
| `--project` | Write settings to `settings.json` even if it already exists |
| `--skip-push-sessions` | Disable automatic pushing of session logs on `git push` |
| `--setup-shell` | Add shell completion to your rc file (non-interactive) |
| `--telemetry=false` | Disable anonymous usage analytics |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Use auto-commit strategy
entire enable --strategy auto-commit

# Force reinstall hooks
entire enable --force

# Save settings locally (not committed to git)
entire enable --local

# Disable session push on git push
entire enable --skip-push-sessions
```
